Opposing: schultz1996 from the SE (~135 deg, toward NW); morgan2006 possible uprange SE +/- 45 deg; Hildebrand et al. 1998 (LPSC abstract, not peer-reviewed; cited by collins2020) from the SW. gulick2008: pre-impact target heterogeneity strongly shapes the asymmetry, so azimuth inferred from structure is uncertain.
parameters.labelEn: Approach azimuth of the impactor (where it came from; clockwise from N)

parameters.label: Gęstość objętościowa impaktora
parameters.locator: collins2020: SI Table 1, Methods; artemieva2009: Sect. 3; christeson2009: Table 1; macke2011: Abstract
parameters.notes: Real density unknown (collins2020 Methods: bulk porosity 'undetermined'). Model values: 2600 (artemieva2009/2017; 'typical for large asteroids with 20-30% porosity'), 2630/2650 (collins2020, internally inconsistent), 2680 (christeson2009). Lower bound 2385 computed from collins2020's statement that Murchison (CM2) bulk density is ~10% below 2650. macke2011: CM/CR meteorites average ~23% porosity. Asteroid-scale macroporosity (rubble pile) could lower bulk density further - speculation, no Chicxulub-specific constraint.
parameters.labelEn: Bulk density of the impactor

parameters.label: Średnica impaktora (skalowanie krateru / modele hydrokodowe)
parameters.locator: collins2020: SI Table 1, Fig. 2-3 captions, Methods; artemieva2017: Sect. 4; artemieva2009: Sect. 3
parameters.notes: Not measured: it is the size that reproduces the observed crater (transient cavity ~90-100 km, seismically constrained) for an assumed speed, angle and density. collins2020 (iSALE3D, 2630 kg/m3): at 20 km/s 12/13/14/16 km for 90/60/45/30 deg; at 12 km/s 16/17/18/21 km. Preferred 45-60 deg -> 13-18 km. artemieva2017: 12.2 km (60 deg, 18 km/s, 2600 kg/m3). artemieva2009: 12 km (90 deg), 14.4 km (45 deg), 16 km (30 deg) at 18 km/s. goderis2021 quotes ~12 km. Baseline 13 km = collins2020 60 deg / 20 km/s. Geochemical (Ir) estimates are smaller: see impactor.diameter_geochem. Synteza: 13 km = rozmiar odtwarzający obserwowany krater w trójwymiarowych symulacjach iSALE dla 20 km/s i 60° (Collins i in. 2020); niezależnie 12,2 km (Artemieva i in. 2017). Prawa skalowania EIEP przy tych wejściach dają krater ~150 km — rozbieżność opisana jako kontrola krzyżowa (crater.final_diameter_eiep, impactor.diameter_for_crater_eiep); hydrokod uznany za wiarygodniejszy od uproszczonego prawa skalowania.
parameters.labelEn: Impactor diameter (crater scaling / hydrocode models)
parameters.notesEn: Not measured: it is the size that reproduces the observed crater (transient cavity ~90-100 km, seismically constrained) for an assumed speed, angle and density. collins2020 (iSALE3D, 2630 kg/m3): at 20 km/s 12/13/14/16 km for 90/60/45/30 deg; at 12 km/s 16/17/18/21 km. Preferred 45-60 deg -> 13-18 km. artemieva2017: 12.2 km (60 deg, 18 km/s, 2600 kg/m3). artemieva2009: 12 km (90 deg), 14.4 km (45 deg), 16 km (30 deg) at 18 km/s. goderis2021 quotes ~12 km. Baseline 13 km = collins2020 60 deg / 20 km/s. Geochemical (Ir) estimates are smaller: see impactor.diameter_geochem. Synthesis: 13 km = the size that reproduces the observed crater in 3D iSALE simulations at 20 km/s and 60° (Collins et al. 2020); independently 12.2 km (Artemieva et al. 2017). EIEP scaling laws with these inputs give a ~150 km crater — the discrepancy is documented as a cross-check (crater.final_diameter_eiep, impactor.diameter_for_crater_eiep); the hydrocode is considered more reliable than the simplified scaling law.
